headline: Data Centers Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, specifically data centers, to pay for the grid infrastructure upgrades their demand necessitates, rather than socializing these costs across all ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Consumer advocates, environmental groups, Governor's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia mulls shifting major grid costs to data centers
news_summary: Virginia regulators are considering how data centers should bear more of the costs for transmission projects, which have historically been spread across all utility customers. Governor Spanberger's administration, along with consumer and environmental advocates, argues that data centers should pay for infrastructure built specifically for their electricity demand.

headline: Mandatory Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that water users supplying data centers report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, provided to these facilities to the State Water Control Board.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, local communities.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, which will be publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to increase transparency regarding the significant water consumption by data centers, especially as groundwater supplies dwindle.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Assessment
short_summary: This law requires local governments to mandate site assessments, including sound profiles, for new high energy use data centers (100 MW or more) before approving rezoning or special permits, giving localities more tools to manage community impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near data center sites, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law
news_summary: Virginia's new law, Section 15.2-2209.5, requires developers of large data centers (100 MW or more) to conduct site assessments, including noise studies, for homes and schools within 500 feet before local approval. While it mandates studies and utility disclosures, it does not set specific noise limits or water caps, leaving the final decision-making power with localities.
